exercises.why: **Зайди** — зайти́ (perfective): to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch; (nautical) to call at, to enter (a port); (nautical) to get, to advance. Wiktionary: за- + -йти́.
exercises.context: Which prefix? The English says which word it is.

exercises.q: What does за- add in заби́ть?
options: an action after which the object ends up behind some boundary, real or imagined
doing the action of the base word in advance, or to store
covering, or being covered, with something
exercises.why: The Russian Wiktionary lists заби́ть under this meaning of за-. Source: Russian Wiktionary, «за-», meaning 4 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/за-).
**забил** — заби́ть (perfective): to drive in (nail), to hammer in, to nail up; to score (a goal); to beat up; to slaughter. Wiktionary: за- + бить.

exercises.q: What does на- add in найти́?
options: (added to nouns or adverbs, forms adverbs with the approximate meaning 'for' the noun or adverb, or in the state of the noun or adverb)
(added to nouns, forms adverbs with the meaning in the direction of the noun)
a quantity of, a lot of
exercises.why: Wiktionary lists найти́ under this meaning of на-. Source: Wiktionary, «на-» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/на-#Russian).
**нашёл** — найти́ (perfective): to find; (figuratively) to think, to consider; to come across; to be located, to be situated. Wiktionary: на- + -йти́.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).

to drive in (nail), to hammer in, to nail up
to throw, to cast, to hurl (somewhere)
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: зайти́ — to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; заби́ть — to drive in (nail), to hammer in, to nail up; забро́сить — to throw, to cast, to hurl (somewhere); забрести́ — (colloquial) to stray, to wander.
